events.label: birth
events.text: Born around 1175, younger son of Bohemond III of Antioch.

evidence.quote: He was born around 1175

events.text: Became Count of Tripoli; father sent him there in late 1187.

evidence.quote: Count of Tripoli from 1187 to 1233
their father sent Bohemond to Tripoli in late 1187

events.text: Marched to Antioch; commune acknowledged his claim to rule.

evidence.quote: In early 1198 , Bohemond marched to Antioch

events.text: Returned to Tripoli shortly after his claim was confirmed.

evidence.quote: Bohemond returned to Tripoli shortly after his claim was confirmed

events.text: Became Prince of Antioch on his father's death; seized the principality.

evidence.quote: Prince of Antioch from 1201 to 1216
After his father died in April 1201 , Bohemond seized Antioch
Bohemond hurried to Antioch when his father died in April 1201

events.label: reconciliation
events.text: Papal legate Gaetani mediated reconciliation with the Hospitallers.

evidence.quote: sent Cardinal Soffred Gaetani to Antioch in late spring 1203
Gaetani mediated a reconciliation between Bohemond and the Hospitallers

events.text: Traveled to Acre and did homage to Marie of Champagne.

evidence.quote: Bohemond traveled to Acre in summer 1204 to meet Marie of Champagne

events.label: injury
events.text: Lost an eye in a battle at the gates of Tripoli.

evidence.quote: Renoart of Nephin pillaged the countryside and led his troops to Tripoli in late 1204
Bohemond lost an eye in a battle at the gates of the town

events.text: Crushed Renoart's rebellion; captured Nephin and Gibelcar.

evidence.quote: He could only crush the rebellion after Aimery died in April 1205
He captured both Nephin and Gibelcar before the end of the year

events.label: patriarch restored
events.text: Restored Eastern Orthodox patriarch Symeon II of Antioch.

evidence.quote: Bohemond restored the Eastern Orthodox patriarch of Antioch , Symeon II , in early 1206 or 1207

events.label: coup
events.text: Sought refuge in the citadel during coup; then captured Latin patriarch.

evidence.quote: Peter of Angoulême helped Raymond-Roupens supporters to return from Cilicia to Antioch in late 1207
Surprised by the coup , Bohemond sought refuge in the citadel
He captured and imprisoned the Latin patriarch who refused to acknowledge him as the lawful prince

events.label: compensation
events.text: Paid compensation to Al-Adil after Hospitaller raids.

evidence.quote: forcing Bohemond to pay a compensation in 1208 or 1209

events.text: Eldest son Raymond murdered by Assassins at Tortosa.

evidence.quote: A group of Assassins murdered Bohemonds eldest son , Raymond , in 1213
was murdered at the Cathedral of Our Lady of Tortosa in 1213

events.text: Cilician troops entered Antioch; Bohemond lost the principality to Raymond-Roupen.

evidence.quote: They helped the Cilician troops to enter Antioch on 14 February 1216
enabled Raymond-Roupen to seize Antioch in 1216

events.text: Married Melisende de Lusignan in Tripoli.

evidence.quote: Andrew attended at the wedding of Bohemond and Hughs half-sister Melisende in Tripoli
Bohemonds second wife , Melisende de Lusignan

events.text: Left the Kingdom of Jerusalem with Andrew II and Hugh I.

evidence.quote: Bohemond left the Kingdom of Jerusalem together with Andrew II of Hungary and Hugh I of Cyprus in January 1218

events.text: Regained the principality of Antioch after Raymond-Roupen was forced out.

evidence.quote: and from 1219 to 1233
Bohemond regained the principality in 1219
In 1219 , a group of Antiochene noblemen rose up against Raymond-Roupen

events.text: Son Philip married Isabella of Cilicia; Bohemond had accepted the offer.

evidence.quote: Bohemond accepted the offer and his son married Isabella in June 1222

events.text: Son Philip murdered in prison; Bohemond could not prevent it.

evidence.quote: could not prevent Philips murder in 1225

events.text: Hurried back to Antioch after son's death and Toghril's invasion.

evidence.quote: could not prevent Philips murder in 1225
After learning of his sons death and Toghrils invasion , Bohemond hurried back

events.text: Joined Emperor Frederick II's gathering of Syrian rulers in Cyprus.

evidence.quote: Bohemond joined him while Frederick was marching from Limassol to Nicosia in August 1228

events.label: meeting
events.text: Met Frederick II again in Acre.

evidence.quote: Bohemond again met Frederick in Acre in 1229

events.label: excommunication
events.text: Pope Gregory IX repeated his excommunication at the Hospitallers' request.

evidence.quote: Pope Gregory IX repeated the excommunication of Bohemond in March 1230

events.label: treaty
events.text: Treaty with the Hospitallers confirmed Jabala and granted money fiefs.

evidence.quote: Bohemond and the Hospitallers made a treaty which was signed on 26 October 1231

events.text: Ceased to be Count of Tripoli.

evidence.quote: Count of Tripoli from 1187 to 1233

events.text: Ceased to be Prince of Antioch (second reign).

evidence.quote: and from 1219 to 1233

events.label: death
events.text: Died in March 1233, a few weeks before the papal confirmation of his treaty.

evidence.quote: Bohemond died in March 1233

Alliance with Az-Zahir Ghazi and Kaykaus I to deter Leo I (no exact date)
Hurried from Tripoli to Antioch to help his brother against Leo I (c. 1194)
Declined to meet papal legate Gaetani (c. 1203)
Excommunicated by the Latin patriarch and Holy See after restoring Symeon II (no exact date)
Expelled Eastern Orthodox patriarch Symeon II from Antioch (no exact date)
Siege of Khawabi lifted and apology sent to Az-Zahir Ghazi (after 1213)
Granted Jabala to the Templars; excommunicated by Pelagius (after 1219)
Repulsed Seljuq attack on Cilicia together with son Philip (1222-1224)
Persuaded Kayqubad I to invade Cilicia (no exact date)
Refused Frederick II's oath of fealty and returned to Nephin (c. 1228)
Excommunication lifted by Gerald of Lausanne; treaty sent to Rome (after 1231)
First marriage to Plaisance, daughter of Hugh III Embriaco (no date)
Succeeded by second son Bohemond in Antioch and Tripoli (after 1233)
